title: A reflective shape factory

blocks.text: A reflective factory maps names to classes and creates instances on demand, so a new shape needs a registration, not a new `switch` branch. Two habits make it robust: **validate at registration** (find the no-arg constructor then, and keep it) rather than when the first `create` fails, and compare names ignoring case **with `Locale.ROOT`**: `toLowerCase()` uses the default locale, and in Turkish `"CIRCLE".toLowerCase()` is `"cırcle"`.

items: `register(name, type)`: remembers `type` under `name`, ignoring case. A `type` with **no no-arg constructor** is refused at once with `IllegalArgumentException`.
`create(name)`: a **new** instance of the class registered under `name` (any case). An unknown name is `IllegalArgumentException`.

rows: `register("CIRCLE", Circle.class)` in a Turkish default locale, `create("circle")`

cases.says: After registering circle and square, create("circle") and create("Square") give new shapes with the right areas, and an unknown name is IllegalArgumentException.
With the default locale set to Turkish, a shape registered as CIRCLE is created as circle.
Registering a shape class that has no no-arg constructor fails at once with IllegalArgumentException.

concepts: A reflective factory maps keys to classes and creates instances on demand, open to new types without new code.
Configuration is validated at startup or registration rather than when the first creation fails, and the found constructor is kept.
